Abbate As Future President And CEO, Effective December 15, Replacing Justin Jude, Who Steps Down Immediate

memos_so_far.headline: LKQ: Q3 adj EPS ~$0.50 vs $0.84, Europe margin halved, CEO out today, guidance withdrawn, restructuring advisers hired
reasoning: Primary source: 8-K items 2.02/5.02/7.01 accepted 12:06 UTC (08:06 ET), Exhibit 99.1 'LKQ Corporation Announces Preliminary Third Quarter 2026 Results and Leadership and Operational Actions'. Benzinga followed at 08:08 ET. No session has traded it.

Quoted: 'Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.47 to $0.53, compared with $0.84 in the third quarter of 2025'; 'Revenue of $3.32 billion, compared with $3.50 billion'; 'Europe parts and services organic revenue decline of 9.8%; and segment EBITDA margin of 4.1% to 5.1%, compared with 10.0%'.

Quoted: 'operational disruptions associated with the ERP implementation in Germany and volume declines in the United Kingdom and Benelux'; 'He succeeds Justin Jude, who is departing the Company effective today'; 'Andy Hamilton is departing his role as President and Managing Director of LKQ Europe'; 'The Board has engaged Alvarez & Marsal ... to advise the Company on its European operations'; 'Withdraws full-year 2026 guidance'.

What changed: earnings power fell about 40% year on year, the CEO and the Europe head are gone at once, the board brought in turnaround advisers, and there is no guidance to anchor estimates. North America 'performed in line'. Full results October 29.
Price: no IEX pre-market trades yet against the 22.465 close.
objections: No pre-market price on our feed: the size of the opening gap is unknown.

memos_so_far.headline: Short LKQ: a multi-quarter European repair with no guidance; estimates get cut after the gap, not before
reasoning: What changed: Europe, about a third of sales, went from a 10% to a ~4.6% EBITDA margin in a year on an ERP failure plus volume declines; the CEO is out with no successor until Dec 15; the board hired Alvarez & Marsal. That combination describes a fix measured in quarters, not weeks.

What the market must believe for the opening gap to be enough: that this is one bad quarter. The release says otherwise: guidance withdrawn, advisers 'with an initial focus on improving customer service levels, stabilizing operations'. Sell-side models cannot be rebuilt until the Oct 29 full report and call, so estimate cuts land over the following days.
Mechanism: large negative surprises that also remove guidance and management tend to keep drifting as holders who own LKQ for steady execution leave over several days.
Direction short, horizon_days 5: covers the Oct 29 report and the first estimate cuts, out before any new CEO plan.

Proves me wrong: LKQ opening down and then reclaiming more than half the gap during the first sessions (the market reading it as a one-off), or the Oct 29 report showing Europe already recovering in October.
objections: No pre-market price on our feed: the size of the opening gap is unknown.
The Oct 29 full report falls inside the horizon and could surprise either way.

memos_so_far.headline: Survives: the gap will be big, but chasing is capped; my last two kills of this kind were wrong
reasoning: Who read it first: an 8-K at 08:06 ET with a CEO exit and withdrawn guidance is read by every desk before the open. Expect a large gap, perhaps -15% to -25%. The question is only whether there is drift after it.

Attack on 'estimates get cut after the gap': analysts can cut immediately on preliminary numbers; the full report on Oct 29 may already be in the price by then. And a stock that falls 20% on a CEO change sometimes rallies on the new CEO's name (Abbate is named, starting Dec 15).
Attack on squeeze risk: shorts after a gap face rebound days; a short is exposed to an outsized move against it if the new CEO is well received.

Track record, which I must weigh: my kills of HAS (long) and EOSE (short) both went on to work (+13.8% and -17.9% respectively). Two cases are below any sample that counts, but both kills of post-news drift trades were wrong, so I raise my bar for objecting.
priced_in_score 0.6. Conditions: the entry must not chase the gap (QUANT's band), and size for a squeeze above the stop.
objections: 1. No pre-market price on our feed: the size of the opening gap is unknown (SCOUT).
2. The Oct 29 full report falls inside the horizon and could surprise either way (ANALYST).
3. Analysts can cut on the preliminary numbers today; drift may be shorter than ANALYST assumes.
4. Squeeze risk on a rebound or a well-received new CEO.
